title: Nigel Farage Skips His Own Victory Party After Winning By-Election
summary:
Imagine winning a big race but not showing up to get your trophy. That's what happened to Nigel Farage, a politician in England. He won a special election called a by-election in the town of Clacton. But when it was time to announce the winner, he wasn't there.

Farage said the police told him about a plan to "disrupt and degrade the result." He didn't want to be "demeaned and humiliated by nobodies." He also worries about his safety. But some people think he skipped the party because he didn't want to answer questions about his party's money problems.

Those money problems are why the by-election happened in the first place. Reform UK, Farage's party, is being investigated by a government watchdog. The investigation is still going on, and Farage might have to answer questions soon. If things go badly, there could be another by-election.

Even though Farage wasn't there, his supporters were happy. He got more votes than he did two years ago. But not everyone in Clacton likes him. Some people think he's too angry and doesn't help himself. A former supporter named Tim Montgomerie said, "When he goes down this angry route he doesn't help himself."

So what happens next? Farage's party says the matter is closed, but the investigation is still open. It's a strange situation: a winner who didn't want to celebrate, and a party that might be in trouble again soon.
why_it_matters: This story shows that winning isn't the end—leaders also have to face hard questions, and how they handle them can affect whether people trust them.
